source.author: Windell Oskay
source.notes: PROBABLY A REPLICA: the photo (Flickr 'Bell Labs 004', 2012) shows the point-contact transistor display at Bell Labs, Murray Hill, New Jersey; Commons titles it 'the first transistor ever made' and a second Commons photo of the same display (File:1st-Transistor.jpg, geotagged at Murray Hill) says 'original exhibited in Bell Laboratories', but the IEEE milestone page describes the Bell Labs Technology Showcase item as 'a replica of Bell Labs' first point-contact transistor' and Invention & Technology credits a 1997 Lucent replica, so treat it as a replica unless Nokia Bell Labs confirms otherwise; no free photo of a confirmed original was found, and no 3D scan exists (Smithsonian, Met, SMG, Sketchfab searched). The device is a germanium slab with two gold-foil contacts on a plastic wedge pressed by a spring, in a Perspex mount about the size of a hand; dimensions are not published by Wikipedia or Bell Labs, so null. Dates from Wikipedia 'Point-contact transistor' (first worked 16 December 1947, demonstrated 23 December 1947).

object.medium: Germanium point-contact transistor: germanium slab, gold-foil contacts on a plastic wedge, spring, Perspex mount
object.description: On 16 December 1947 John Bardeen and Walter Brattain of Bell Telephone Laboratories made a slab of germanium amplify an electrical signal by pressing two closely spaced gold contacts against its surface. Their point-contact transistor, demonstrated to Bell executives a week later, was the first working transistor and the ancestor of every semiconductor device since. The device shown is the display at Bell Labs in Murray Hill, generally identified as a replica of the original.
facts: The critical experiment on 16 December 1947 used a block of germanium with two very closely spaced gold contacts held against it by a spring.
Brattain made the two contacts by slitting a strip of gold foil wrapped over the point of a plastic triangle, leaving a gap of less than 0.1 mm.
The invention was demonstrated to Bell Labs management on 23 December 1947 and announced publicly in June 1948.
